CHAPTER.VERS: I declare but to you, brethren, the glad tidings which I announced as glad tidings to you, which also you received, in which also you have stood,
through which also you are being saved; (by a certain word I announced as glad tidings to you if you retain;) except if not inconsiderately you believed.
I delivered for to you among first things what also I received; that Anointed died on behalf of the sins of us, according to the writings;
and that he was buried, and that he was raised the third day, according to the writings;
and that he was seen by Cephas, then by the twelve.
After that he was seen above by five hundred brethren at once, out of whom the greater number remain till now, some but also have fallen asleep.
After that he was seen by James; then by the Apostles all.
Last and of all, just as if by the abortion, he was seen also by me.
(I for am the least of the apostles; who not am fit to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the congregation of the God.
By favor but of God I am what I am; and the favor of him that to me, not vain was made, but more abundantly of them all I labored; not I but, but the favor of the God that with me.)
Whether therefore I, or they, thus we proclaim, and thus you believed.
If but Anointed is proclaimed, that out of dead ones has been raised, how say some among you, that a resurrection of dead ones not is?
If but a resurrection of dead ones not is, not even Anointed has been raised;
if but Anointed not has been raised, void then the preaching of us, void and also the faith of you.
We are found and even false witnesses of the God; because we testified concerning the God, that he raised up the Anointed, whom not he raised up, if indeed dead ones not are raised up.
If for dead ones not are raised up, not even Anointed has been raised;
if but Anointed not has been raised; deceptive the faith of you; still you are in the sins of you;
then also those having fallen asleep in Anointed, perished.
If in the life this having been hoping we are in Anointed alone, more pitiable of all men we are.
Now but Anointed has been raised up out of dead ones, a firstfruit of those having fallen asleep.
Since for through a man the death, also through a man a resurrection of dead ones.
As for in the Adam all die, so also in the Anointed all will be made alive.
Each one and in the own band; a firstfruit Anointed, after that those of the Anointed, in the presence of him;
then the end, when he should have delivered up the kingdom to the God and Father, when he should have abrogated all government and all authority and power.
It behooves for him to reign, till he may have placed all the enemies under the feet of him.
Last enemy is rendered powerless the death;
all things for he subjected under the feet of him. When but it may be said, that all things have been subjected, it is evident, that is excepted the one having subjected to him the all things.
When but may be subjected to him, the all things, then also himself the son will be subject to the one having subjected to him the all things so that may be the God the all things in all.
Otherwise what shall they do those being dipped on behalf of the dead ones, if at all dead ones not are raised up? why and are they dipped on behalf of them?
Why and we are in danger every hour?
Every day I die, by the your boasting, which I have in Anointed Jesus the Lord of us.
If according to man I fought with a wild beast in Ephesus, what to me the profit? if dead ones not are raised up, we may eat and we may drink; tomorrow for we die.
Not be you led astray. Corrupt habits virtuous companionships evil.
Awake you as it is fit, and not sin you; ignorance for of God some have; for shame to you I speak.
But will say some one: How are raised up the dead ones? in what and body do they come?
O foolish one; thou what sowest, not is made alive, if not it should die;
and what thou sowest, not that body that going to be born thou sowest, but a naked grain, if it may happen, of wheat, or some of the others;
the but God to it gives a body as he willed, and to each of the seeds the own body.
Not all flesh, the same flesh; but one indeed of men, another and flesh of cattle, another and of fishes, another but of birds.
And bodies heavenly, and bodies earthly; but one indeed that of the heavenlies glory, another and that of the earthlies.
One glory of sun, and another glory of moon, and another glory of stars; a star for from a star differs in glory.
Thus and the resurrection of the dead ones. It is sown in corruption, it is raised in incorruption;
it is sown in dishonor, it is raised in glory; it is sown in weakness, it is raised in power; it is sown a body soulical, it is raised a body spiritual.
Is a body soulical, and is a body spiritual.
So and it has been written: Was made the first man Adam into a soul living; the last Adam into a spirit lifegiving.
But not first the spiritual, but the soulical; afterwards the spiritual.
The first man, from earth earthy; the second man, the Lord from heaven.
Of what kind the earthy, such like also the earthy ones; and of what kind the heavenly, such like also the heavenly ones;
and even as we bore the image of the earthy, we shall bear also the image of the heavenly.
This and I say, brethren, that flesh and blood a kingdom of God to inherit not are able, nor the corruption the incorruption shall inherit.
Lo, a mystery to you I speak: All indeed not we shall be asleep; all but which we shall be changed,
in a moment, in a twinkling of an eye, in the last trumpet. (It shall sound for, and the dead ones shall be raised incorruptible, and we shall be changed.)
It is necessary for the incorruptible this to be clothed with incorruption, and the mortal this to be clothed with immortality.

When but the corruptible this shall be clothed with incorruption, and the mortal this shall be clothed with immortality, then will happen the word that having been written: Was swallowed up the death into victory.
Where of thee, O death, the sting? where of thee, O unseen, the victory?
The but sting of the death, the sin; the and power of the sin, the law.
To the but God thanks, to the one having given to us, the victory through the Lord of us Jesus Anointed.
Wherefore, brethren of me beloved, steadfast be you, unmovable, abounding in the work of the Lord at all times, knowing, that the labor of you not is vain in Lord.
